subject: science

entries: Light and sound are different kinds of waves: light is transverse, so a particle bobs across the direction of travel, while sound is longitudinal, so the particles bunch and spread along the direction of travel.
slots.label: Wave types
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength: for any wave, v = f x wavelength - for sound in air, 340 m/s = 170 Hz x 2 m.
slots.label: Wave equation
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: we see lightning before we hear thunder: reject the claim that sound outruns light - light is far faster, so the flash arrives first and the thunder follows seconds later.
slots.label: Check the thinking
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: What the wave examples have in common: every wave carries energy while its particles only vibrate in place, and speed, frequency and wavelength always obey v = f x wavelength.
slots.label: What waves have in common
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A disturbance that carries energy from place to place without carrying matter with it: the particles vibrate in place while the energy moves on.
slots.label: Wave
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A wave whose vibration is across the direction of travel, like light: a particle on the wave bobs up and down while the wave races sideways.
slots.label: Transverse wave
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A wave whose vibration is along the direction of travel, like sound: the particles bunch together and spread apart as the wave passes.
slots.label: Longitudinal wave
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: How many full waves pass a point each second, measured in hertz (Hz): a frequency of 170 Hz means 170 waves per second.
slots.label: Frequency
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The length of one full wave, from one crest to the next, measured in metres: the sound wave in this lesson has a wavelength of 2 m.
slots.label: Wavelength
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: Waves: light, sound and the wave equation
